question: Bank of Canada Decision in October?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the target for the overnight rate resulting from the October 2026 interest rate announcement of the Bank of Canada, relative to the level it was prior to this announcement.

The resolution source will be official information from the Bank of Canada, including the statement or release from its October 2026 interest rate announcement, scheduled for October 28, 2026, as listed on the official Bank of Canada calendar (https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/#target-dates). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Bank of Canada resulting from its October 2026 interest rate decision with relevant data is issued. 

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound. 

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified announcement is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled announcement, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed announcement.  If the specified announcement is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled announcement, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified announcement will not be considered.
research:
The policy rate was 2.25% going into the October 28 meeting, and nothing published by October 14 settled the outcome. As of that date, markets priced roughly a 27% to 33% chance of a 25 bp hike and treated a hold as most likely.

## 1. Resolution source
- The Bank of Canada's key interest rate page is the source. Some search results and pages I came across are dated after 2026-10-14, and I have left them out.
- 2025-10-29: the target for the overnight rate was cut to 2.25%. That is the level going into the October 28, 2026 announcement. Earlier cuts: 2.75% on 2025-07-30 and 2.50% on 2025-09-17. [BoC](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/)
- The announcement is scheduled for 2026-10-28, together with the October Monetary Policy Report (MPR). [BoC Sept release](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/09/fad-press-release-2026-09-02/)

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-10-14)
- Nothing has settled the question. The rate is 2.25%, and the debate is between a hold and a 25 bp hike. I found no source discussing a cut.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-13/14: big-bank year-end 2026 forecasts:
  - RBC, TD and BMO: 2.25%, meaning no hike in 2026.
  - Scotiabank and National Bank: 2.50%, meaning one hike.
  - [nesto](https://www.nesto.ca/mortgage-basics/mortgage-rates-forecast-canada/)
- 2026-10-09: the September jobs report was weak.
  - Canada lost 68,000 jobs against an expected gain of 9,200. Unemployment rose to 6.5%, after about 42,000 jobs were lost in August.
  - TD's Andrew Hencic said two months of weak labour data argue against near-term hikes.
  - [Advisor.ca](https://www.advisor.ca/economy/economic-indicators/canada-sheds-68000-jobs-unemployment-rate-up-to-6-5-in-september/), [Investment Executive](https://www.investmentexecutive.com/news/canada-sheds-68000-jobs-unemployment-rate-up-to-6-5-in-september/)
- 2026-10-01/02: market odds of an October hike fell to about 1 in 3, after a weak US jobs report and a coordinated release of emergency oil stocks on October 2. [nesto](https://www.nesto.ca/mortgage-basics/mortgage-rates-forecast-canada/)
- Late September 2026: other forecasters leaned more hawkish. Manulife Investment Management expected hikes at the next two meetings, and Capital Economics moved its first-hike call forward to as early as December. [nesto](https://www.nesto.ca/mortgage-basics/mortgage-rates-forecast-canada/)
- 2026-09-15 (approx.): August inflation data.
  - Headline CPI was 3.0% year over year, as expected. Gasoline was up 22.8% and CPI excluding gasoline was 2.4%.
  - The Bank's core measures were near target: CPI-trim 1.9%, CPI-median 2.0%.
  - RBC's base case was a hold through the end of 2026.
  - [RBC](https://www.rbc.com/en/economics/canadian-analysis/data-flashes/canadian-inflation-holds-at-3-in-august-as-underlying-pressures-remain-contained/), [MPA](https://www.mpamag.com/ca/mortgage-industry/industry-trends/canadas-august-cpi-holds-as-october-boc-decision-nears/589650)
- 2026-09-02: the Bank held at 2.25%, its seventh straight hold.
  - CPI was around 3%, driven by gasoline, which the Bank tied to the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz still being largely closed. Excluding gasoline, CPI was 2.2% in July.
  - The Bank said upside risks to inflation had increased and that it "is prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed."
  - [BoC](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2026/09/fad-press-release-2026-09-02/)

## 4. Base rates
- The Bank has held at 2.25% at seven straight meetings, from December 2025 through September 2026. Its last change was the 25 bp cut on 2025-10-29. [BoC](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/core-functions/monetary-policy/key-interest-rate/)
- Past moves in this cycle were 25 bp each, and I found no recent precedent for a 50 bp move. A move in either direction would break a long run of holds. The last hike was in July 2023.
- October meetings come with an MPR. Historically the Bank prefers to change rates at MPR meetings, but I did not find a statistic quantifying this.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-10-09: TD Economics said markets priced about a 27% chance of an October hike and about 88% for a hike by December. [nesto](https://www.nesto.ca/mortgage-basics/mortgage-rates-forecast-canada/)
- Early October: overnight index swaps priced about 100 bp of increases over the next 12 months. [nesto](https://www.nesto.ca/mortgage-basics/mortgage-rates-forecast-canada/)
- Late September: odds of an October hike were near 50%. One Morningstar report around mid-September cited a 76% probability for the "next meeting". I could not open that page to check its date or exact wording. [Morningstar via search](https://global.morningstar.com/en-ca/economy/cpi-shows-inflation-is-contained-elevated-heres-what-that-means-interest-rates)
- 2026-10-09: on Polymarket, "No Change" led at about 83%, with $158K traded. That figure comes from the PredScope aggregator, not Polymarket's own page. Another mirror page with very thin volume ($1.4K) showed No Change 87%, a 25 bp increase 10% and a 25 bp decrease 10%. Those numbers don't add up and look unreliable. [PredScope](https://predscope.com/event/bank-of-canada-decision-in-october-20260715203359314), [mirror](https://polymarkets.co.il/en/market/bank-of-canada-decision-in-october-20260715203359314/)
- I did not find a Kalshi or Manifold price dated before October 14.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-10-19 (date not confirmed in sources): Bank of Canada Q3 Business Outlook Survey and Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations, with inflation expectations as a key input.
- About 2026-10-15 to 19: IMF/World Bank annual meetings, where Governor Macklem may speak.
- About 2026-10-20 (date not confirmed in sources): September CPI. The Bank's stated trigger is whether high energy prices spread into broader inflation, so core and ex-gasoline measures matter most.
- Oil prices and Strait of Hormuz developments, plus US and Canadian tariff news. The Bank cited new US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs as possible cost pressures.
- 2026-10-28: decision and MPR.

forecasts.reasoning:
gly against a hike.
- **2026-10-09, market pricing:** TD reported markets pricing about a 27% chance of an October hike, down from about 50% in late September. Polymarket "No Change" stood at about 83%, which is a fairly liquid anchor with matching wording.
- **Mid-September, August CPI:** Headline was 3.0%, driven by gasoline. Core measures were near target (trim 1.9%, median 2.0%).
- **2026-09-02, last decision:** The Bank flagged upside inflation risk and said it was "prepared to adjust."
- **2026-10-13/14, bank forecasts:** RBC, TD and BMO see a hold through year-end. Scotiabank and National Bank expect one hike, likely in December.

**(e) Unexpected-outcome scenarios:**
- **Hike:** The September CPI around October 20 shows energy prices spreading into core measures, and the Business Outlook Survey shows inflation expectations unanchoring. The Bank then hikes 25 bp at the MPR meeting.
- **Cut:** Further labour deterioration and an oil price collapse after the reserve release push the Bank to cut. This looks unlikely given that no source discusses easing.

**Reasoning:**
- I anchor on Polymarket at about 83% hold and about 15-17% hike.
- The weak jobs data has largely been priced in by now, but it plus near-target core inflation make an October hike hard to justify. Most hike expectations are centred on December.
- I stay close to the market, with a small residual for a cut and for tail outcomes.

- **Bank forecasts:** RBC, TD and BMO expect no hike in 2026. Scotiabank and National Bank expect one hike, probably in December rather than October.
- **No source mentions a cut.**

**(e) Unexpected scenario:** September CPI (about October 20) shows core measures jumping and energy prices spreading into broader inflation. Business Outlook Survey inflation expectations also come in elevated. The Bank then uses the October MPR meeting to deliver a pre-emptive 25 bp hike despite the weak labour market. Alternatively, a sharp collapse in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz reopens, combined with a deepening job slump, could push a dovish surprise, though a cut is very unlikely so soon after hawkish language.

**Reasoning:** I start from the market anchor of roughly 75 to 83% No Change and about 20 to 27% for a hike. I moved slightly toward hold because the severity of two consecutive weak jobs reports, and the fact that core inflation is at target, make an October hike hard to justify. Swaps may still embed some term premium from the energy shock. However, the September CPI release still to come is a real source of hawkish risk, so I keep a meaningful hike probability. I leave small tails on a cut and on a 50 bp move in either direction.
